title: Independence of a regular-sequence kernel from the regular-local presentation
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ be a Noetherian complete local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $q_0:P\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $q:Q\twoheadrightarrow A$ be surjective local homomorphisms from regular local rings $(P,\mathfrak m_P)$ and $(Q,\mathfrak m_Q)$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Then $\ker q_0$ is generated by a finite $P$-regular sequence contained in $\mathfrak m_P$ if and only if $\ker q$ is generated by a finite $Q$-regular sequence contained in $\mathfrak m_Q$. Empty sequences are allowed.

source.place: Tag 09PZ (lemma-ci-well-defined), equivalence of “some” and “every” regular-local surjection onto a complete Noetherian local ring.

proof.text: The kernels of $q_0$ and $q$ are finitely generated ideals in the respective maximal ideals, since regular local rings are Noetherian. Complete $P$ and $Q$ at their maximal ideals. Apply completion-regular-kernel-preservation to each kernel, identifying its quotient with $A$. Since $A$ is already complete, the canonical completed quotient is again $A$; that lemma supplies the surjective maps from the completions and equivalences of the original and completed kernel conditions. Completion-regular-local makes both completions regular local with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_P\widehat P$, $\mathfrak m_Q\widehat Q$; adic-completion-mod-ideal (1) makes them complete for these. A surjection onto the local ring $A$ is local. So it suffices to compare complete regular local sources.

source.place: Tag 09PZ, proof, second paragraph (reduction to complete sources).

proof.text: Fix once and for all a Cohen presentation $c_0:T_0=\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\twoheadrightarrow A$ from the cited presentation theorem. Its statement supplies locality, the complete regular local source and the coefficient-ring characteristic alternative, so the same fixed $c_0$ can be used for both completed presentations. In the field case its residue-field isomorphism forces $\operatorname{char}(\Lambda)=0$, as required by the lifted-square lemma.

source.place: Tag 09PZ, proof, first paragraph; Algebra 032A, 032C; More on Algebra 07NL.

proof.text: For either completed surjection $r:R\twoheadrightarrow A$, put $J=\ker r$. This ideal lies in $\mathfrak m_R$ and has finite generators $b_1,\ldots,b_s$, since $R$ is regular local and hence Noetherian. Apply the lifted-evaluation-square lemma to these generators and the fixed $c_0$. It gives complete regular local $T=T_0[[y_1,\ldots,y_s]]$, a surjective local $\pi:T\to T_0$ and local maps $f:T_0\to R$ and $h:T\to R$, with $rf=c_0$, $h|_{T_0}=f$ and $rh=c_0\pi$, together with the adic evaluation formula for $h$.

source.place: Tag 09PZ, proof, third paragraph, adding variables and constructing the commutative square; More on Algebra 07NL universal property.

proof.text: Apply homogeneous-preimages with $C=T_0$, $I=\mathfrak m_R$, the lift $f$ and evaluation $E=h$. By steps 1 and 3, $R$ is $\mathfrak m_R$-adically complete and $b_j\in\mathfrak m_R$. Its quotient-surjectivity hypothesis holds as $R/J\cong A$ and $rf=c_0$ is surjective. Step 3's evaluation formula is exactly its formula. It yields homogeneous approximations and a formal-series preimage of every $z\in R$, so $h$ is surjective (also when $J=0$, $s=0$).

source.place: Tag 09PZ, proof, third paragraph, details of the claimed surjectivity (formal-series limit).

proof.text: Apply regular-local-surjection-kernel-comparison to $T\xrightarrow{h}R\xrightarrow{r}A$: these maps are surjective local and $T,R$ are regular local. It equates the regular-sequence kernel conditions for $r\circ h$ and $r$. Apply the same lemma to $T\xrightarrow{\pi}T_0\xrightarrow{c_0}A$: here $\pi$ is surjective local by evaluation at zero, and $T,T_0$ are regular local. It equates the kernel conditions for $c_0\circ\pi$ and $c_0$. The equality $r\circ h=c_0\circ\pi$ now yields the equivalence of the kernel conditions for $r$ and $c_0$. Do this for each of the two completed sources; both compare with this one fixed $c_0$. Chaining the two equivalences and undoing step 1 proves the item. All kernels lie in the respective maximal ideals, and the comparison includes empty sequences.
